items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: Al Bartee came up to me and said, 'Man, I'm working at a place in North...up in Hollywood, called the Tailspin, with Georgie Auld. We need a bass player. Can you make the gig?'

ctx.x: And after they went past a point to prove what they were trying to prove, I was OK. Guys were shaking my hand, and patting me on the back, 'Yeah, yeah.' Because at one point, when the tune was up like that, after the horn players took... whatever...they left it open for me to solo. And I knew right then I had to outshine anything I'd ever done. Because here somebody's putting me through a test. I didn't.

But it came out great. I succeeded and I was accepted. And that's the way...Al Bartee came up to me and said, 'Man, I'm working at a place in North...up in Hollywood, called the Tailspin, with Georgie Auld. We need a bass player. Can you make the gig?' And I said I was looking for a gig, yeah. And he said, 'Oh, this is great, man,' he said. So he got ahold of George and the next day George called me to work this job.
So you didn't have any trouble getting a job.
